Lorsqu’on a annoncé que Québec solidaire: When it was announced that Québec solidaire was holding a joint conference with La France Insoumise on the very night of the leaders’ debate, we were all curious in the newsroom. In this federal campaign, many voters, especially on the left, are wondering whether to vote strategically, whether to stay true to their convictions and whether the left can win.
À La Converse, on considère que couvrir: At La Converse, we believe that covering politics shouldn’t be limited to polls, campaign ads and scripted exchanges between party leaders. It is just as crucial to look at the ideas, the tensions and the surges of hope that move voters at this particular moment in democratic life.
Je me suis donc rendue sur place pour re: So I went there to meet those who chose to attend this event, rather than watch the Canadiens game, and to hear what they had to say. I also wanted to document an event organized by a left that, despite its divisions and doubts, is trying to bring people together and inspire engagement.
<strong>Alors que le débat des chefs et: While the leaders’ debate and the Canadiens game dominated screens on Wednesday night, more than 400 people made a different choice: attending a joint conference with Ruba Ghazal and Jean-Luc Mélenchon in the heart of Montréal. The sold-out evening at La Maison Théâtre was held under a single rallying cry: “Beat the Right.” Our report.
« Ne vous étonnez pas, si vous abandonne: “Don’t be surprised, if you leave your ideas at the door of the polling station, that you don’t find them in the ballot box,” Jean-Luc Mélenchon told a packed house at La Maison Théâtre. The last time the leader of La France Insoumise (LFI) visited Quebec was in 2016. Nine years after his last visit to Montréal, the French politician is back in force, in a context marked by federal elections.
Dès 17 h, la file s’étire dans le Quarti: By 5 p.m., the line was stretching through the Quartier des spectacles. More than 1,000 people had registered, according to Québec solidaire. In the crowd: students, retirees, activists, undecided voters… and the curious. All had come to see a political figure who leaves no one indifferent: Jean-Luc Mélenchon. Here, no one hesitated to answer the joint call from Québec solidaire and La France Insoumise, despite the busy lineup of the evening.
« Honnêtement, le hockey, je ne suis pas: “Honestly, I’m not really into hockey, and the leaders’ debate is boring, so I wouldn’t have watched it even if I’d had nothing else planned. We know exactly what’s going to be said, which is not much,” says Imane, a thirty-something who works in communications. Fred, for her part, has just come out of a three-hour exam. “It’s a chance to hear Mélenchon in person. I want to know what they’re going to say about strategic voting. I’m a bit torn… about whether I should vote strategically or go with my values and vote NDP,” confides the sexology student. She is, in fact, hesitating over giving her vote to the Liberal Party to stop the Conservative Party.
Ce dilemme entre vote de conviction et v: This dilemma between voting on principle and voting strategically comes up in several conversations. Denis, a longtime former activist, has a lot on his chest: “Québec solidaire has drifted away from its base. They used to listen to people, now they act out of electoral calculation,” he says bluntly. The 69-year-old retiree hopes to see a stronger, more radical Quebec left emerge, like the conference’s guest. In the meantime, Denis will vote NDP, even though he doesn’t think the party is able to win the election.

Même désenchantement chez Rayan, 20 ans,: Rayan, 20, a Quebecer whose parents emigrated from Algeria, feels the same disenchantment: “The problem with Québec solidaire and the left here is that there are lots of conflicts within the party itself, and people trust them less and less. In France, LFI seems more united to me. And Mélenchon gives me hope,” says the young man, his eyes on his phone’s wallpaper, which is a picture of the French politician. He discovered Jean-Luc Mélenchon four years ago when he became interested in French politics and “fell for him.” Delighted that he was in Montréal, he didn’t want to miss the chance to hear him.

À l’ouverture des portes à 18 h, l’effer: When the doors opened at 6 p.m., the buzz turned into momentum. The 400-seat hall filled up quickly. Some people sat on the steps. The atmosphere was electric. QS director Myriam Fortin opened the evening. “It warms my heart to see so many people wanting to talk about the left and about how to beat the right,” said the Charlevoix native before welcoming Ruba Ghazal.
La co-porte-parole entre en scène, accue: The co-spokesperson came on stage to an ovation. “You saw the poster, ‘Beat the Right,’ with Ruba Ghazal and Jean-Luc Mélenchon, and you said to yourselves: ‘Where do I sign up? I have to hear Ruba Ghazal!’ That’s why there are so many people, of course!” she joked humbly, aware that most of those present had come to hear her French counterpart.
Pendant une trentaine de minutes, elle d: For about thirty minutes, she laid out a blunt reading of the Quebec and Canadian political landscape. “The rise of the right has many faces, it takes many forms, but make no mistake,” the MNA warned. “It always uses the same language: the language of exclusion, of hatred of immigrants, of rejection of social progress, of turning inward and the law of the strongest!” said Ruba Ghazal. She named in turn Putin, Trump, Poilievre and his “reactionary, populist and conservative right,” and Legault, whom she accused of building a “narrow” vision of the Quebec people.
Sous les applaudissements nourris d’un p: To the loud applause of an audience already on her side, she hammered home the values the left must defend without compromise in the face of the danger that right-wing policies would pose: the environment, women’s rights, on which these right-wing forces would wage “a war,” Indigenous rights, housing, health…
« Les constats que je pose ici pour le Q: “The observations I’m making here about Quebec, Jean-Luc saw coming long before, several years ago in France. Yet today we can see where French politics stands. We’re not there in Quebec,” said Ruba Ghazal, before urging everyone to get involved by donating to the party, joining it or becoming active. She then gave way to the “highlight of the show.”

Vêtu d’un costume noir agrémenté d’une c: Dressed in a black suit with a red tie, the colour of La France Insoumise, Jean-Luc Mélenchon walked on stage like a rock star. The audience, warmed up by a Ruba Ghazal in top form, gave the French politician an ovation. A smile spread across the face of a man who knows he enjoys a certain popularity among Quebecers. “I’m here because this is a Québec solidaire rally, and because La France Insoumise is tied to Québec solidaire, for better or worse, in mutual respect, in friendship and in the fraternity of struggle,” he said in his opening remarks.
Puis, il se lance dans un exercice inatt: Then he launched into an unexpected exercise, addressing a message to the American president in English, a language he considers “poor” and one that does not “allow for in-depth thinking.” Despite a pronunciation that was sometimes hesitant, he delivered a monologue that was both politically charged and funny. “You said that Canada should become an American state. All the Canadian leaders told you they are opposed. They said ‘no.’ And ‘no’ means ‘no,’ in English as in French!” Mr. Mélenchon explained as if speaking to a child.
Il enchaîne, faussement sérieux : « En t: He went on, with mock seriousness: “As French people, we support Canada and Quebec. And I can tell you, most Europeans think the same. Right now, we support Ukraine, which has been invaded by Russia. We would also support Canada and Quebec if they were invaded. The United States too, for that matter. Fortunately, no one is threatening you.” The playful jab drew laughter and applause from the audience.

L’Insoumis conclut cette parenthèse en a: The La France Insoumise leader ended this aside by saying that while European leaders “are afraid” of Trump, he is ready to repeat all this to him “to his face” if he wishes. Jean-Luc Mélenchon is in fact heading to New York this Thursday, April 17, as part of the promotional tour for his new book, Faites mieux ! Vers la révolution citoyenne, which has been translated into English.
Le politicien de 73 ans, dont l’énergie: The 73-year-old politician, whose energy does not seem to fade with the years, then resumed his argument about the need for a return to the foundations of the left.
« Être de gauche nécessite une forme d’i: “Being on the left requires a form of intransigence. Not so much toward others, but toward yourself,” said the man who is often at the centre of controversy for his positions. But according to Mr. Mélenchon, it is fidelity to one’s values, whatever the commentators say, that explains LFI’s growing success in France.
Durant 45 minutes, celui dont les talent: For 45 minutes, a man whose talents as an orator no longer need proving sent a clear message to his audience: the left must “own itself,” “accept being divisive,” “make no concessions.” Several times, Jean-Luc Mélenchon cited Kamala Harris as an example of what the left must not be, arguing that repeated concessions weakened voters’ confidence in her political ability to offer an alternative, and led to Donald Trump’s re-election.
Il enjoint les Canadiens de gauche, tout: He urged left-wing Canadians to stay true to their convictions, while insisting he had no intention of interfering. Without ever uttering the words, he clearly denounced strategic voting, which he considers counterproductive: “If you leave your ideas at the door of the polling station, don’t be surprised that you don’t find them in the ballot box, don’t be surprised,” declared the man who has not yet confirmed whether he intends to run in France’s next presidential election.
Pour clôturer la soirée, Ruba Ghazal rej: To close the evening, Ruba Ghazal joined Jean-Luc Mélenchon on stage and asked him a few questions in a conversation tinged with complicity. He explained why the Francophone world and social media must be embraced in order to allow an international union of left-wing forces, the only way, in his view, to stand up to the rise of the far right. However, no concrete proposal for making this union possible was clearly put forward during the evening.
Depuis plusieurs années, plusieurs déput: For several years now, a number of La France Insoumise MPs have in fact turned into full-fledged YouTubers, racking up millions of views. “That doesn’t stop us from going on traditional media, but it lets us speak directly to voters, and we can see that it works,” he said. According to Mr. Mélenchon, you can criticize Elon Musk while staying on X, because “you have to be where the people are, otherwise you can no longer talk to them.”
Des conseils qui ont rapidement germé da: The advice quickly took root in Ruba Ghazal’s mind: “So, MNAs, are you going to launch your YouTube channels?” she asked the elected members present in the hall before closing the evening. The audience, visibly won over by the performance of two political figures who have a lot in common, gave her one last ovation.
Dans le hall de La Maison Théâtre, la so: In the lobby of La Maison Théâtre, the evening continued around information booths. Québec solidaire took the opportunity to solicit donations and attract new members, while La France Insoumise offered Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s book at a discounted price. It was a strategy that paid off.
Tania, 29 ans, passe à l’action : « J’ét: Tania, 29, took action: “I was a sympathizer, but tonight, I’m joining. We complain a lot, but we do little. Tonight, I decided to get involved.” Mission accomplished for Ghazal and Mélenchon: a breath of hope for a left that is searching for itself, but not giving up.
